answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because quill only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any plume approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
